line: That last session ran long, but I'd have listened to more. What did you make of it?
followUps: Which part will you actually use?
Was it what you expected going in?
shareBack: Offer the one point you took from the session, in a sentence, then ask what they are heading to next.
deliveryCue: At a conference or talk, in the minutes after a session ends.

line: Mind if I join you? I've been hovering by the coffee long enough.
followUps: What were you talking about before I arrived?
How has the event been for you so far?
shareBack: Add one short line on what you have enjoyed so far, then pick up their topic again.
deliveryCue: At a conference or party. Say it lightly, then listen before adding much.

line: I don't know many people here yet, so I thought I'd come and say hello. What brought you along?
followUps: Have you been to one of these before?
What's been the best part so far?
shareBack: Mention in a sentence how you ended up here, then ask who else they have met.
deliveryCue: Good for someone standing alone. Smile and leave a little space.

line: The food line seems to be where everyone ends up. Spotted anything I shouldn't miss?
followUps: Have you been to one of these before?
Are you an early-arrival person at these things?
shareBack: Say what you are hoping is still left, then ask what else they have tried.
deliveryCue: At a party, conference, or wedding with a buffet.

line: I liked the question you asked in that session. It was the one I wanted answered. What made you ask it?
followUps: Did the answer settle it for you?
Is that something you deal with a lot?
shareBack: Offer why the question mattered to you, in a sentence, then ask what else they are going to.
deliveryCue: At a conference or class, soon after the session.

line: Which session are you most looking forward to? I'm still working out my plan.
followUps: What drew you to that one?
Is there anything you plan to skip?
shareBack: Name the one session you have circled and why, then ask if they would like to compare notes later.
deliveryCue: At a conference, early in the day.

line: What kind of work brings you to an event like this?
followUps: What does a normal week of that look like?
How did you get into it?
shareBack: Give your own work in one plain sentence, then ask what they hope to take home from the event.
deliveryCue: At a professional event only. At a party, ask something else.

line: Working on anything interesting right now?
followUps: What's the part you're enjoying most?
How did that one come about?
shareBack: Offer one thing you are working on, with one detail they can pick up, then hand the turn back.
deliveryCue: At a work event, or once they have mentioned their work.

line: I came mostly for the afternoon talks, and I'm already glad I did. What's been the best thing you've heard so far?
followUps: What made that one stand out?
Would you go and hear that speaker again?
shareBack: Share the one idea you wrote down today, then ask what they are going to next.
deliveryCue: At a conference. Swap in the talks you came for.

line: Good to see you again. I think we last talked at one of these. What's kept you busy since?
followUps: How did that turn out?
What's next on your list?
shareBack: Offer one thing that has changed for you since then, in a sentence, then ask about their plans.
deliveryCue: When you run into them again at the next event.

line: You seem to know your way around this event. Is there a talk or a stand I shouldn't miss?
followUps: What did you like about it?
How many times have you been?
shareBack: Say what you came hoping to find, then ask what keeps them coming back.
deliveryCue: At a conference, fair, or festival.

line: I'm new to this group, so I'm still learning who everyone is. How did you get involved?
followUps: What has kept you coming back?
Who else should I say hello to?
shareBack: Mention how you heard about the group, in a sentence, then ask what is coming up next for it.
deliveryCue: At a club, class, or meetup you have just joined, or in its group chat.

line: I'm trying to work out how everyone here knows the hosts. What's your connection?
followUps: How long have you known them?
What were they like back then?
shareBack: Say how you know the hosts, with one small detail, then ask if they know many others here.
deliveryCue: At a party.

line: I've gone back for this twice already. Have you tried it, or is there something better I've missed?
followUps: Do you cook much, or mostly appreciate?
What's the best thing you've eaten lately?
shareBack: Offer one dish you make or always order, then ask what they would recommend.
deliveryCue: Say it with the plate in your hand.

line: Anything you're looking forward to in the next few weeks?
followUps: What are you most excited about with that?
How did that come about?
shareBack: Offer one thing you are looking forward to, in a sentence, then ask another question about theirs.

line: Seen, read or watched anything good lately? I'm short on recommendations.
followUps: What did you like about it?
What should I start with?
shareBack: Offer one thing you enjoyed recently and why, in a sentence, then ask what else is on their list.

line: Is this your kind of party, or are you more of a quiet-dinner person? I can never decide.
followUps: What does a good evening look like for you?
What's the best gathering you've been to lately?
shareBack: Say which one you lean toward and why, in a sentence, then ask about their plans for the weekend.
deliveryCue: At a party. Keep it playful.

line: It looks like we're table neighbors for the evening. Do you know anyone else at this table, or are we all new?
followUps: How do you know the hosts?
Have you been to this place before?
shareBack: Say in a sentence who you came with or how you were invited, then ask about their evening so far.
deliveryCue: At a wedding or seated dinner, as you sit down.

line: I always enjoy these more than I expect to. What's been your favorite moment so far?
followUps: What made that one stand out?
Who have you enjoyed talking to?
shareBack: Offer your own favorite moment in a sentence, then ask what they are doing afterwards.
deliveryCue: At a party, wedding, or celebration.

line: What's something you've got into lately that you didn't expect to enjoy?
followUps: How did you come across it?
What's the appeal, now you're in it?
shareBack: Offer one thing you have picked up lately, with a detail, then ask what they want to try next.

line: Last time we talked, it sounded like you had a lot on. Has life calmed down or sped up since?
followUps: What's taking most of your attention now?
What's been the good part of it?
shareBack: Say in a sentence how your own last few months have gone, then go back to what they told you.
deliveryCue: Only if they mentioned being busy. Say it warmly, then give them time.

line: I'm still piecing together who belongs to whom. How do you know the couple?
followUps: What were they like when you first met them?
Do you have a favorite story about them?
shareBack: Say how you know the couple, with one small detail, then ask who else they know here.
deliveryCue: At a wedding.

line: That ceremony was beautiful. Was there a part that got you?
followUps: Had you heard that story before?
How long have you known the two of them?
shareBack: Name the moment that stayed with you, in a sentence, then ask how they know the family.
deliveryCue: At a wedding, soon after the ceremony.

line: The speeches were better than most I've heard. Which one was your favorite?
followUps: Did you know that story already?
Have you ever had to give one yourself?
shareBack: Say which line made you laugh, then ask how they know the person who gave it.
deliveryCue: At a wedding or party, after the speeches.

line: Days like this remind me of the big gatherings I grew up with. What were family events like for you?
followUps: Who was always at the center of them?
Is there one you still think about?
shareBack: Offer one short memory of a gathering from your own family, then ask what today reminds them of.
deliveryCue: At a wedding or family party, once you have talked a few minutes.

line: While we wait for the others: anything good happen for you this week?
followUps: What made that the good part?
Is the rest of the week looking as good?
shareBack: Offer one small good thing from your own week, in a sentence, then ask what they have coming up.
deliveryCue: On a call or in a room, while you wait for others to join.

line: Looks like we're the early ones. Have you worked with this group before?
followUps: How did you come to join?
Who here should I get to know?
shareBack: Say in a sentence how you ended up on the call, then ask what they hope gets covered.
deliveryCue: When you are early to a meeting, workshop, or call.

line: Are you joining from home or an office today? I'm at my kitchen table.
followUps: What's the best thing about your setup?
Do you get out much between calls?
shareBack: Add one small detail about where you are sitting, then ask how their day is shaping up.
deliveryCue: On a video call, in the first minute.

line: What are you hoping to get out of this session? I'm mostly here to listen.
followUps: What made you sign up?
Have you been to one of these before?
shareBack: Name the one question you would like answered, then ask what they are working toward.
deliveryCue: At a workshop, class, or talk, before it starts.

line: I'm early in learning this field. If you were starting now, what would you focus on first?
followUps: What makes that the place to start?
What would you leave for later?
shareBack: Say in a sentence where you are right now and what you have tried, then ask what they would do next.

line: What are you reading or paying attention to right now?
followUps: What made you pick that up?
Has it changed how you see anything?
shareBack: Mention one thing you are reading or following, in a sentence, then ask what they would suggest next.

line: I've followed your work for a while, and the way you explain things has helped me. How did you learn to do that?
followUps: Did someone teach you, or was it trial and error?
What did the early attempts look like?
shareBack: Name the one explanation of theirs that helped you and what you did with it, then hand the turn back.
deliveryCue: Be specific about what helped; keep it to one sentence.

line: Is there a book or a person that shaped how you work? I'm building a reading list.
followUps: What did you take from it?
When did you come across it?
shareBack: Offer the one book or person that has shaped you so far, then ask what they would add after it.

line: Your talk gave me a lot to think about, especially the part on what didn't work. What made you include that?
followUps: How did people react at the time?
What would you add if you gave it again?
shareBack: Say in a sentence what you plan to try because of the talk, then ask what they are working on now.
deliveryCue: After their talk. Keep it brief; others may be waiting to speak to them.

line: What's one habit you'd suggest to someone who wants to get better at this work?
followUps: How did you build that habit yourself?
What gets in the way of it?
shareBack: Mention one habit you already keep and how it is going, then ask what they would add to it.

line: I'm deciding what to learn next, and you came to mind as someone to ask. What skill has paid off most for you?
followUps: How did you go about learning it?
When did you notice it paying off?
shareBack: Say which two skills you are choosing between, in a sentence, then ask which they would pick.

line: What's caught your attention at this event so far? I'd trust your pick over the program.
followUps: What was good about it?
Is there anything you think is overrated?
shareBack: Say which session you got the most from, then ask what they are going to next.
deliveryCue: At a conference or festival.

line: What's the most useful thing you've learned recently?
followUps: How did you come across it?
What have you done differently since?
shareBack: Offer one useful thing you learned lately, in a sentence, then ask what they want to learn next.

line: Who did you learn the most from when you were starting out?
followUps: What did they do that others did not?
Is there something of theirs you still use?
shareBack: Mention one person who has taught you a lot and what you took from them, then hand the turn back.

line: I won't talk shop all night, but your work has taught me a lot. What are you enjoying outside of it lately?
followUps: How did you get into that?
What do you like most about it?
shareBack: Offer one thing you enjoy outside work, with a detail, then ask what they would recommend trying.
deliveryCue: At a party. Keep the thanks to one sentence, then let work go.

line: Thanks for making time; I've been looking forward to this. What would make the conversation useful for you too?
followUps: What are you curious about right now?
How do you like to run these?
shareBack: Say in a sentence the one thing you hope to leave with, then ask where they would like to start.
deliveryCue: In the first minute of a coffee or call they agreed to.

line: It was good to meet you today. One thing you said has stayed with me. Is there one thing you'd suggest I read next?
followUps: What did you take from it yourself?
May I tell you what I think once I've read it?
shareBack: Reply with one line on what stayed with you and why, then thank them.
deliveryCue: Send the same day. Name the thing they said if you can.

line: Thank you for the advice earlier. I tried it and it helped. No need to reply; I just wanted you to know.
followUps: Is there a next step you would suggest?
What did you find hardest when you first tried it?
shareBack: If they reply, say in one line what you tried and what changed.
deliveryCue: Send only once you have tried it.

line: I just read something that made me think of your work. May I send it over?
followUps: Does it match what you have seen?
What would you add to it?
shareBack: Send it with one line on why it made you think of them, and leave it there.

line: Quick question, no rush: what's one thing you're reading or listening to that you'd recommend?
followUps: What did you like about it?
What should I look out for in it?
shareBack: Reply with thanks and one thing you have enjoyed lately, in a single line.

line: I saw your latest piece of work and learned a lot from it. What was the hardest part to get right?
followUps: How did you get past it?
Would you approach it the same way again?
shareBack: Reply with the one thing you learned from it, in a line, and thank them.
deliveryCue: Name the piece of work so it is clear you looked at it.

line: Would you be open to a 15-minute call sometime this month? I have two specific questions and I'll keep it short.
followUps: What day suits you best?
Would you like the questions in advance?
shareBack: If they agree, send the two questions in one short message so they can think ahead.
deliveryCue: Have the two questions written before you send this.

line: Thanks for talking with me today. I'm going to try what you suggested this week. May I tell you how it goes?
followUps: Is there anything I should watch for as I try it?
When would be a good time to check back?
shareBack: When you report back, give one line on what happened and one on what you learned.
deliveryCue: Send the same day, while the conversation is fresh.

line: It's been a while. Something you taught me came in handy today and I thought of you. Hope things are going well.
followUps: What are you working on these days?
Is there anything I can do for you?
shareBack: If they reply, say in one line what happened and how their lesson helped.
deliveryCue: Ask nothing in the first message; let them choose how much to reply.

line: Something you told me keeps coming back to me. When you faced a big choice, what helped you decide? A line is plenty.
followUps: Did it feel clear at the time?
Is there something you would weigh differently now?
shareBack: Reply with the choice you are facing, in one line, and thank them for the steer.

line: How did you decide to move into the work you do now?
followUps: What nearly stopped you?
When did you know it was the right call?
shareBack: Say in a sentence what you are weighing in your own work, then ask what they would look at first.
deliveryCue: Once you know their line of work.

line: Looking back, what do you wish you'd known earlier in your career?
followUps: How did you end up learning it?
Would you have listened if someone had told you?
shareBack: Offer one thing you have already learned the hard way, in a sentence, then hand the turn back.

line: Is there a work decision you'd make differently if you had it again?
followUps: What do you know now that you did not then?
What did it teach you?
shareBack: Mention one decision of your own you are unsure about, briefly, then ask how they would look at it.
deliveryCue: Ask with curiosity, not as a test.

line: I'm stuck on a decision about my next step. How do you think through choices like that?
followUps: What do you look at first?
Who do you talk it over with?
shareBack: Lay out your two options in a sentence each, then ask what they would want to know before choosing.

line: It seems like you've stayed curious about this work for a long time. What keeps it interesting?
followUps: Was there a time it stopped being interesting?
What are you curious about right now?
shareBack: Say what first drew you to the work, in a sentence, then ask what they would explore in your place.

line: First time in this class? I'm still figuring out where everyone puts their things.
followUps: What made you sign up?
Have you done anything like it before?
shareBack: Say in a sentence what got you to sign up, then ask what they hope to get out of it.
deliveryCue: At a class, before it starts.

line: This line had better be worth it. Have you been here before?
followUps: What do you usually get?
Is it always this busy?
shareBack: Say what you're hoping to get and why, then ask what they'd recommend.
deliveryCue: Waiting in line at a cafe, show, or food truck.

line: That looks like a good book. Is it worth the wait in here?
followUps: What made you pick it up?
What else have you read lately that you liked?
shareBack: Mention one book you've enjoyed lately, in a sentence, then ask what they'd read next.
deliveryCue: In a waiting room or on a train, and only if they look open to talking.

line: I just found out where the good snacks are hiding. Want the tip?
followUps: Do you know many people here?
What brought you out tonight?
shareBack: Say in a sentence how you ended up at the party, then ask who else they've met.
deliveryCue: At a party. Point the way with a smile.

line: The band is better than I expected. Are you a dancer, or more of a watcher like me?
followUps: What song would get you on the floor?
What's the best band you've heard at one of these?
shareBack: Admit in a sentence which song would get you dancing, then ask theirs.
deliveryCue: At a wedding or party with music.

line: Looks like we both found the quiet corner. Is this your first time at one of these?
followUps: What's been worth coming for so far?
Do you like big events, or smaller ones?
shareBack: Say how you like to pace yourself at these things, in a sentence, then ask what is next on their day.
deliveryCue: At a busy event, in a quieter spot.

line: I'm not great at this part, so I'm just going to say hi. I'm glad to meet you.
followUps: What brought you here today?
What's been the best part of your day so far?
shareBack: Offer one easy detail about how you came to be here, then ask what brought them.
deliveryCue: Works anywhere. Say your name after it and let them take it from there.

line: The high point of my week was finally fixing my bike. What's been the best part of yours?
followUps: What made that the good part?
Is the rest of the week looking as good?
shareBack: Add one small detail about your own good moment, then ask what they have coming up.
deliveryCue: Swap in your own small win.

line: Is there a place around here you'd send a friend who's visiting for the day?
followUps: What makes it worth the trip?
Is there a spot you're saving for a special occasion?
shareBack: Offer one local place you like and what to order there, then ask what else they'd add.
deliveryCue: Best at a local event, not a destination one.

line: Hi! I think we're at the same table for Saturday's dinner. Looking forward to meeting you.
followUps: Have you been to one of these before?
Do you know many people going?
shareBack: If they reply, say in a line how you know the hosts or organizers, then ask how they do.
deliveryCue: Swap in the real event. Send a day or two before.

line: Hi, we're in the same class this term. Did you catch what's due for next week?
followUps: How are you finding it so far?
Have you taken anything with this teacher before?
shareBack: Mention in a line what drew you to the class, then ask what they're hoping to get from it.
deliveryCue: For a class group chat, or a direct message to a classmate.

line: Saw your question in the event chat. I was wondering the same thing. Did you ever find out?
followUps: Are you going to that session?
Is this your first time at this one?
shareBack: Say in a line what you're most hoping to catch at the event, then ask about their plan.
deliveryCue: In an event app or group chat, before or during the event.

line: Hi, looks like we'll both be at Thursday's workshop. Any idea what to bring, or are we winging it?
followUps: What made you sign up?
Have you done one of these before?
shareBack: Say in a line what you're hoping to learn there, then ask what they're hoping for.
deliveryCue: Swap in the real event.

line: Nice to share the wait with someone. Good luck with the rest of your day.
followUps: Anything good planned for the rest of the day?
shareBack: Say in a line what's next for you, and wish them well.
deliveryCue: At the end of a wait in line or in a waiting room.

line: Good to meet you tonight. Enjoy the rest of your weekend.
followUps: Did you end up staying late?
Anything good planned for the weekend?
shareBack: If they reply, add one line on what you enjoyed about meeting them, then leave it there.
deliveryCue: Send that night or the next morning.

line: Saw this and thought of what you said the other night. No need to reply, just passing it on.
followUps: Did you end up going?
What did you think of it?
shareBack: If they reply, say in a line why it made you think of them, then ask one thing about it.
deliveryCue: Add the link, and name what they said if you can.

line: Hope tomorrow goes well! You sounded ready for it.
followUps: How did it go?
What was the best part?
shareBack: If they write back afterward, say in a line that you're glad, then ask what's next.
deliveryCue: Only if they mentioned something coming up.

line: Okay, totally new topic: what's the best thing you've eaten this month?
followUps: Where was it?
Would you go back for it?
shareBack: Name your own best meal of the month, in a sentence, then ask what else is on their list.
deliveryCue: Own the switch with a smile.

line: Here's a random one: is there something you've been meaning to try for ages?
followUps: What's been in the way so far?
What would it take to finally do it?
shareBack: Offer one thing you keep meaning to try, in a sentence, then ask what got them interested in theirs.

line: We've talked about the hosts for ten minutes and I still don't know what you like doing on a free weekend.
followUps: How did you get into that?
What's the best part of it?
shareBack: Offer one thing you like doing on a free day, in a sentence, then hand it back.
deliveryCue: Say it with a laugh once the talk about the hosts runs dry.

line: What's a small thing you've changed your mind about lately? Mine is coffee. I used to hate it.
followUps: What changed it for you?
Is there anything you still hold out on?
shareBack: Say in a sentence what finally won you over, then go back to theirs.
deliveryCue: Swap in your own small example; keep it small so they keep it small too.

line: What's been keeping you busy lately, outside of work?
followUps: How did you get into that?
What's the best part of it?
shareBack: Offer one thing keeping you busy outside work, in a sentence, then hand the turn back.

line: Picking up from the party: did you ever try that place you mentioned?
followUps: Was it as good as you hoped?
What should I order if I go?
shareBack: Say in a line whether you've been, then ask what they'd recommend.
deliveryCue: Swap in the real place or plan they mentioned.

line: You said something earlier that stuck with me. How did you get into that?
followUps: What kept you going with it?
What surprised you about it?
shareBack: Offer one thing you've stuck with for a while, in a sentence, then go back to theirs.
deliveryCue: Name the thing they mentioned. A follow-up beats a new question.

line: What's something you're hoping to do more of this year?
followUps: What got you thinking about it?
What's the first step?
shareBack: Offer one thing you'd like more of this year, in a sentence, then ask a question about theirs.

line: What's a skill you picked up that turned out more useful than you expected?
followUps: How did you learn it?
Where has it come in handy?
shareBack: Offer one skill of your own that surprised you, in a sentence, then hand the turn back.

line: Is there a moment from the last year you'd happily live again?
followUps: What made it so good?
What did it lead to?
shareBack: Offer one moment from your own year you'd repeat, in a sentence, then hand the turn back.

line: You light up when you talk about that. It sounds like it matters to you.
followUps: How did it start?
What's the best part of it for you?
shareBack: Say in a sentence what matters to you in the same way, then hand the turn back.
deliveryCue: Only if it is true. Then pause and let them choose how much to say.

line: What's the best piece of advice you've been given?
followUps: Who gave it to you?
When has it come in handy?
shareBack: Offer the best advice you have been given, in a sentence, then ask whether they agree with it.

line: I keep thinking about what you said the other night. What got you started on it?
followUps: What's kept you at it?
Is there more to that story?
shareBack: If they reply, offer one line on why it stuck with you, then ask one more thing about it.
deliveryCue: Name what they said so it is clear you were listening.

line: I think we met at the last one of these. Did that trip you were planning happen?
followUps: What was the highlight?
Would you go back?
shareBack: Offer one thing that's happened for you since you met, in a sentence, then ask what's next for them.
deliveryCue: Swap in what they told you last time.

line: I tried the cafe you told me about. You were right about the pastries.
followUps: What else should I try?
How did you find it in the first place?
shareBack: Say in a sentence what you ordered and liked, then ask what they've been up to since.
deliveryCue: Swap in the real recommendation.

line: We sat next to each other at the wedding! Did you make it to the end of the dancing?
followUps: What was your favorite part of the night?
How do you know the couple again?
shareBack: Say in a sentence what you remember best from the night, then ask what they have been up to since.
deliveryCue: When you run into someone from a recent event. Swap in the real one.

line: Didn't we meet at the conference in the spring? I remember your question on the panel.
followUps: Did you ever get the answer you wanted?
Are you going to the next one?
shareBack: Say in a sentence what you took from that event, then ask what they are here for today.
deliveryCue: Swap in the real event and what you remember.

line: Great to meet you at the conference. I looked up the book you mentioned; it's on my list now.
followUps: What did you like most about it?
Anything else you would add to the list?
shareBack: If they reply, say in a line what drew you to it, then ask one more thing about it.
deliveryCue: Send within a day or two. Swap in the real detail.

line: It was really nice talking with you on Saturday. Good luck with everything you have coming up.
followUps: How did it all go?
shareBack: If they reply, add one line about your week, then ask one thing about theirs.
deliveryCue: Swap in what they mentioned, if you can.

line: We met at the workshop a few months ago, and something you said came up today. Hope things are going well!
followUps: What have you been up to since then?
Did you end up going back?
shareBack: If they reply, say in a line what came up and how their point helped.
deliveryCue: Ask nothing in the first message; let them choose how much to reply.

line: Enjoyed meeting you at the class. Same time next week?
followUps: Did you get through the homework?
Want to grab seats together?
shareBack: If they reply, say in a line what you liked about the class, then ask what they thought.
deliveryCue: For a weekly class or club.

line: I'd like to keep talking about this. Want to swap numbers?
followUps: What's the best way to reach you?
shareBack: Give your number or handle first, so they don't have to ask.
deliveryCue: Near the end, while the talk is still going well.

line: Are you coming to the next one? It'd be good to see a familiar face.
followUps: Do you know when it is?
Want to go together?
shareBack: Say in a sentence which one you're planning to go to, then suggest meeting by the door.
